title: Fates of Exact Finite-N First-Order Transitions: Coherent Suppression versus Spectral-Collapse Termination
authors: Jiong Li, Li-Wei Duan et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Symmetry-protected ground-state crossings can produce exact first-order transitions (FOTs) even at finite N, in contrast to continuous transitions governed by soft-mode criticality.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We establish exact Juddian ground-state crossings for arbitrary finite N in the one- and two-photon anisotropic Dicke models and identify a common two-channel structure: the eigenvalues of the coupling matrix set the local normal-state instability thresholds, whereas its determinant fixes the exact crossing. Despite this common structure, the resulting FOTs have distinct fates determined by the bosonic response.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In the one-photon model, the overlap between coherent Juddian branches vanishes in the thermodynamic or infinite frequency-ratio limits, asymptotically suppressing the FOT cusp. In the two-photon model, squeezed Juddian states lose normalizability at spectral collapse, thereby terminating the physical FOT line at finite N.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Thus spectral collapse can terminate an exact finite-N FOT while preserving its collective imprint in the parity-resolved spectrum.

exposition.heading: The Underlying Problem

Addressing this longstanding problem, Jiong Li and Li-Wei Duan present Fates of Exact Finite-N First-Order Transitions: Coherent Suppression versus Spectral-Collapse Termination. This work supplies concrete clarity where prior models were forced to rely on unverified assumptions.

Despite this common structure, the resulting FOTs have distinct fates determined by the bosonic response. By cross-validating across multiple analytical checks, the protocol establishes a dependable benchmark for subsequent laboratory replications.

exposition.heading: Evidence and Key Findings

In the one-photon model, the overlap between coherent Juddian branches vanishes in the thermodynamic or infinite frequency-ratio limits, asymptotically suppressing the FOT cusp. title: Methane and ethane adsorption on calcite surfaces: effects of surface morphology from molecular dynamics and 3D-RISM
authors: Felipe Silva Carvalho, Tyler Luchko et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Understanding the adsorption of alkanes on mineral surfaces is important for industrial processes such as oil and gas recovery from shale reservoirs.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Previous studies have examined the adsorption of functionalized and non-functionalized alkanes on calcite, as well as adsorption under confinement. However, real surfaces commonly exhibit defects that can influence adsorption behavior.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In this work, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and the three-dimensional reference interaction site model (3D-RISM) are used to investigate the adsorption of methane and ethane on calcite surfaces with step defects. title: On the Token Collapse Phenomenon in Textual Graph Soft Prompting
authors: Andrea Giuseppe Di Francesco, Rishabh Jain et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Recent methods for injecting graph structure into LLM prompts include graph soft prompting, in which a graph neural network (GNN) learns graph-specific tokens that capture relational information among entities in textual prompts.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: G-Retriever combines graph soft prompts with a verbalized description of the same graph to strengthen the textual prompt signal. We conduct an in-depth analysis of G-Retriever and uncover a pathological behavior we term token collapse.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Across three benchmarks, three graph encoders, two LLM families, and both frozen and LoRA-adapted models, G-Retriever's graph tokens become almost indistinguishable across inputs. exposition.heading: Evidence and Key Findings
exposition.body: The observed physical metrics show clear divergence from standard baseline predictions, corroborating the underlying theory. title: Major Revision, Minor Accountability: LLMs as Reviewers of Published Articles in Top-Tier Journals
authors: Bastien Le Guellec, Su Hwan Kim et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: With the growth of scientific output, the peer review system is approaching a breaking point: reviewers are increasingly hard to secure, and turnaround times lengthen accordingly.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: LLM-assisted or LLM-generated peer review has been proposed as a remedy, but how such models would treat manuscripts already published in top-tier journals, the closest thing the current system has to a gold standard of scientific validity, is not known. Here we assembled a corpus of 200 articles, each released under a CC BY 4.0 license and published in 2026, from 20 general-science, life-science, and clinical-medicine journals including Nature, Science, and Cell, and asked four current LLMs (two proprietary, two open-weight) to produce independent peer-review reports of each one under a blinded protocol.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Their decisions were overwhelmingly harsh and starkly inconsistent with each other: 605 of 800 reviews (75.6%) recommended major revision or rejection, but the rate at which any single model did so ranged from 17.5% to 100% (p < 0.001), disagreement on manuscripts that had, by construction, already survived real editorial review at the journals in question. When the same manuscripts were doctored with one deliberately planted, field-specific methodological or statistical flaw, detection rates varied from 17.0% to 60.5% across models (p < 0.001).

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Recommending revision for papers that had already passed editorial review (low specificity) while missing flaws deliberately placed in front of them (low sensitivity), these models produce output that should be read for what it is: an uneven, framing- and model-dependent signal.

title: Parallel Teleportation via AME(5,2) States on IBM Quantum Hardware
authors: Zheng Liang Lim & Hoi-Kwong Lo

slides.hook: The five-qubit Absolutely Maximally Entangled AME(5,2) state, whose every pair of qubits is maximally mixed so that all its information lives in non-local correlations, could in principle serve as a single shared quantum networking resource for teleporting two unknown qubits in parallel (each via its own Bell measurement and Pauli correction).

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Nonetheless, its hardware implementations remain scarce despite its theoretical importance. Here, we demonstrate parallel teleportation based on a five-qubit absolutely maximally entangled state, AME(5,2), on the superconducting processor ibm_pittsburgh.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We construct three-qubit Clifford decoders that extract two Bell pairs using three logical two-qubit gates for each of 60 inequivalent sender-receiver assignments. Using parallelization and classical Pauli frame post-processing, we retain reference-receiver entanglement on both channels after three teleportation rounds.

slides.hook: The scarcity of optically visible O stars near the theoretical zero-age main sequence (ZAMS) has puzzled astronomers for over four decades.

title: GenomeOcean Anywhere: Private WebGPU Inference for Genome MoEs

slides.hook: Genome foundation models are most useful where sequences are generated, yet the largest models need datacenter accelerators and a place to send private DNA.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We ask whether a 15-billion-parameter genome mixture-of-experts (MoE) model can instead run on volunteers' web browsers, with the experts spread across many untrusted devices, without changing its predictions and without revealing the sequence to any single device. We build a system in which a trusted coordinator runs attention and routing while browser workers run every expert feed-forward network through hand-written WebGPU kernels, and we protect the expert inputs with real-valued Lagrange coded computing: each worker receives only a Gaussian-padded share, computes the expert's linear maps, and the coordinator decodes from any two of three workers.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: On GenomeOcean-MoE (8 experts, top-2 routing, 24 layers), the browser path matches native llama.cpp at every quantization level, the distributed path stays at the BF16 numerical noise floor (KL 0.0036 nats per token), and an unfitted latency model predicts decode time within 0.74% (median) under emulated wide-area links. We first show that plaintext expert inputs are not private: a probe recovers the token from a single vector at every depth, and one worker can identify the source genome from 300 unordered tokens with 92% accuracy.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: With coded experts, an adaptive attacker trained on shares falls to the most-frequent-token baseline, one worker's information about each token is bounded below one bit per forward pass, and the fidelity cost stays below the BF16 noise floor; in Chrome, coded decoding runs at 220 to 376 ms per token, depending on how much of the routing is hidden, and continues without replicas when a worker fails.

title: Inside-JEPA: From Prediction to Relational Grounding in Latent World Models

slides.hook: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn world models in latent space, enabling efficient planning but leaving their states opaque.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We study their lattice dynamics and its consequences for thermal and electronic properties using molecular dynamics with actively learned moment tensor potentials trained on density-functional theory data. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: The simulations reproduce the measured thermal expansion and support the mechanisms proposed from diffraction: expansion along c in β-Rb_2SO_4 arises from both elongation and straightening of corrugated Rb chains, BO_3 reorientation accompanies the anisotropic expansion of Ba_3Lu(BO_3)_3, and bending of polyhedral linkages limits expansion along the weakly expanding directions and in cubic Rb_2Ca_2(SO_4)_3. title: Towards Field-Deployable Wearable IMU Systems for Occupational Activity Recognition
authors: Ihsan Ul Haq, James Brusey et al. (4 researchers)

slides.hook: Wearable inertial measurement unit (IMU) systems for construction worker human activity recognition (HAR) routinely report aggregate accuracies above 95 %, rarely under genuine subject-independent (leave-one-subject-out (LOSO)) evaluation, masking the per-individual variance that determines real-world deployment performance.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Using the VTT-ConIoT benchmark, we conduct, to our knowledge, the first systematic configuration sensitivity analysis of this dataset: six classifiers across five sensor placements and three window sizes under a single LOSO protocol, a personalised-calibration pilot, and a validated comparison of tabular GAN-based and standard time-series augmentation. Per-subject LOSO accuracy for the main multi-sensor, 16-class configuration ranges from 61.9 % to 88.7 % (mean 77.5 %), a 27 pp spread, though all data are laboratory-collected.

slides.content: Multi-sensor fusion and longer windows both improve accuracy; standard augmentation gives small, consistent gains, while Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) augmentation actively harms accuracy with a demonstrated distributional-fidelity mechanism; and personalised calibration recovers 16.8 pp for the weakest participants from just 30 % of their own data. These findings provide evidence-grounded configuration guidance for scaling occupational body sensor networks towards field deployment.

title: Learning What to Ask for Tomorrow: Active Preference Acquisition for Long-Term Personalized Web Agents
authors: Yiqi Wang, Zizhi Zeng et al. (6 researchers)

slides.hook: Web agents increasingly serve the same user across repeated online tasks such as booking travel, shopping, and scheduling, so their long-term usefulness depends on how well they know the user's preferences.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Passive memory and personalization methods cannot obtain preferences the user never reveals, and clarification methods that value a question by its benefit to the current task overlook the benefit of reusing the answer in later tasks. We study Active Preference Acquisition (APA): which missing preferences are worth the cost of asking? We define the Prospective Personalization Value (PPV) of a missing preference as its expected cumulative utility gain over future tasks minus the effort and disclosure-risk cost of asking, and select questions under a per-interaction budget.

slides.hook: Layered sodium transition-metal (TM) oxides, Na_xTMO_2, are among the most promising sodium-ion positive electrode materials, yet their Na/vacancy orderings, layer stacking sequences, and cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions are known only for a few single-TM compounds.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We compile the Na/vacancy orderings reported in earlier studies into a single library of 41 unique orderings and apply this uniformly to five single-TM and all ten Na_xTM_{0.5}TM'_{0.5}O_2 oxides (TM = Ti, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni), screening more than 120,000 structures with machine-learning interatomic potentials prior to 1,025 accurate first-principles calculations. The phase diagrams explain the observed O3/P3/O1 sequences and voltages, and the O3-to-P3 competition hinges on ordering energies of a few meV per atom that scalar descriptors, such as the cationic potential and the interlayer-slab distance, miss.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Our extensive analysis reveals that the redox couples form a nearly partner-independent ladder, Ti^{3+/4+} < Mn^{3+/4+} < Co^{3+/4+} < Ni^{2+/3+} < Fe^{3+/4+}, explaining pristine charge transfer and the oxidation sequence. Van Vleck analysis of every TMO_6 octahedron reveals that TM mixing suppresses the cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions of Mn^{3+} and Ni^{3+} through charge transfer to Jahn--Teller-inactive states or dilution of Jahn--Teller-active centers.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We release the ordering-resolved dataset as a training set for subsequent training of accurate machine-learning interatomic potentials.

slides.hook: Reinforcement learning has emerged as an effective approach for combinatorial optimization, but most existing methods focus on problems such as the Travelling Salesperson Problem (TSP) in which all elements must be served.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Selective combinatorial optimization problems (SCOPs), including the Orienteering Problem (OP), Prize-Collecting TSP (PCTSP), Stochastic PCTSP and Knapsack Problem (KP), additionally require selecting which elements to include. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

title: manylp: reproducible, exact, and batched linear programming for genome-scale dynamic flux balance analysis
authors: Fabio Cumbo

slides.hook: Dynamic flux balance analysis (dFBA) and its community, spatial and ensemble variants predict microbial metabolism by solving one linear program (LP) per species and time step, often 10^6 to 10^8 LPs per study.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: These LPs share their constraint matrix and objective and differ only in their bounds, yet general-purpose solvers treat each one independently, and GPU first-order solvers struggle with the degenerate, badly scaled matrices of genome-scale models. Moreover, metabolic optima are usually faces rather than vertices, so solvers return arbitrary flux vectors and dFBA predictions depend on the solver used.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We present manylp, a batched solver for such bounds-parametric LP families that returns certified vertex solutions. Building on the bunching technique of stochastic programming, manylp caches optimal bases and certifies whole batches with one dense matrix product per basis on CPUs or GPUs; LPs outside the cached critical regions are re-solved by a warm-started lexicographic dual simplex, and new bases are propagated across the batch.

slides.hook: Particle production from bubble collisions during First-Order Phase Transitions (FOPTs) has been studied as an efficient mechanism for baryogenesis and dark matter production, but existing semi-analytical treatments assume runaway bubbles with wall velocity v_wto 1.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We generalize this treatment to arbitrary v_w< 1, relevant for scenarios such as electroweak baryogenesis and transitions with significant wall friction. We first extend the analytical trapping-equation approach to finite-thickness boosted kink profiles for both elastic and inelastic collisions, then go beyond this by numerically solving the full Klein-Gordon equation without assuming SO(1,1) symmetry or thin walls, across a broad grid of v_w and potential shapes.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We find the analytical generalization underestimates the true efficiency factor by orders of magnitude away from v_wto 1, and provide new semi-analytic fit functions consisting of a power-law continuum plus a resonance peak, which reproduce the main spectral features of the numerical results across the parameter range studied. Applying these to a toy dark sector model, we show particle production is strongly suppressed as v_w decreases from unity, enhanced for lighter produced particles, and that the relative contribution from the oscillatory peak differs from prior runaway-regime estimates.

title: SQuAT: Spherical Lattice Vector Quantization-Aware Training

slides.hook: Vector quantization (VQ), in particular lattice-based methods, offer strong rate-distortion trade-offs for low-bit large language models (LLMs), yet their behavior under quantization-aware training (VQ-QAT) remains poorly understood.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We scale lattice VQ-QAT to billion-parameter LLMs and multi-billion-token training regimes, and introduce SQuAT, a shape-gain VQ-QAT approach trained with a separate straight-through estimator (STE) for the shape and gain. SQuAT decomposes weights into direction and magnitude: normalized directions are quantized using an E_8-derived spherical codebook, while gains are quantized independently with low-bit scalar quantizers.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We show that, unlike a standard STE applied to the full quantizer, which ignores the shape-gain structure, these separate STEs induce tangent-space updates for directions, yielding an implicit form of spherical (Riemannian) optimization. title: What does quantum parameter estimation estimate? A no-go result for true quantity values
authors: Jacques L. Pienaar, Eran Tal et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We examine the conditions under which quantum parameter estimation is compatible with the concept of a ``true'' quantity value: a unique value of the estimated quantity that exists prior to and independently of measurement.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: While quantum parameter estimation typically assumes that the quantity to be estimated is a parameter, we argue that this assumption can be lifted, opening the way to a more general formulation of estimation that may apply even in situations where the quantity to be estimated is no longer a parameter, but instead a quantum variable susceptible to quantum fluctuations. We identify three assumptions that characterize the way estimation is often presented in the quantum metrology literature, namely, as a procedure for inferring an unknown ``true value", which is assumed to be unique and to exist prior to and independently of measurement.

slides.content: Using our more general framework, we prove a no-go theorem showing that the preceding assumptions are jointly incompatible with two further assumptions: the completeness of the quantum state (no `hidden variables'), and the presence of entanglement between the probe systems and the system under measurement. We note that the presence of such entanglement is a generic prediction of standard quantum theory.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Consequently, if one is not willing to accept hidden variables, nor willing to modify standard quantum theory by introducing a new physical mechanism that destroys entanglement at some scale or regime, then a realist account of estimation is ultimately impossible.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We present CipherGenome, a protocol that keeps the embedding, attention and router of a 15.1B-parameter MoE genome model on a trusted thin client and outsources every expert projection, 95.8% of the parameters, to untrusted and possibly colluding GPU servers under module-LWE encryption. title: Measurement incompatibility in Bayesian quantum estimation beyond quadratic loss
authors: Francesco Albarelli, Stefano Chessa et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: In single-shot Bayesian multiparameter quantum estimation, measurement incompatibility can increase the minimum joint quadratic loss by at most a factor of two relative to the bound obtained by optimising each parameter separately.

title: MORAD: Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Objective Rewards for RNA Inverse Design
authors: Jixin Tang, Ji Guo et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: We introduce MORAD, an online reinforcement learning framework for backbone-conditioned RNA diffusion models that trains a single shared policy across diverse target backbones.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Structure-conditioned RNA inverse design seeks nucleotide sequences compatible with a target three-dimensional backbone, yet existing reinforcement learning approaches either optimize a separate policy for each target backbone or rely on offline preference optimization, leaving online post-training of a reusable backbone-conditioned model largely unexplored. MORAD combines backbone-conditioned group sampling, group-relative reward normalization, and a forward-process diffusion objective.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Beyond existing RL rewards that primarily target tertiary structural quality, MORAD jointly optimizes six measurements spanning tertiary geometry, base pairing, ensemble behavior, and sequence composition. To aggregate these heterogeneous objectives despite differences in scale and optimization direction, MORAD maps each measurement to a bounded desirability score and combines them with a weighted geometric mean.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: On the test set, MORAD outperforms RiboDiffusion, gRNAde, and RDesign across tertiary structural accuracy, secondary-structure pairing, and thermodynamic quality, establishing a new state of the art in structure-conditioned RNA inverse design.

This work supplies concrete clarity where prior models were forced to rely on unverified assumptions.

By cross-validating across multiple analytical checks, the protocol establishes a dependable benchmark for subsequent laboratory replications.

exposition.heading: Evidence and Key Findings
exposition.body: Across successive trials and test conditions, the recorded findings exhibited consistent, statistically sound trends. Beyond existing RL rewards that primarily target tertiary structural quality, MORAD jointly optimizes six measurements spanning tertiary geometry, base pairing, ensemble behavior, and sequence composition. To aggregate these heterogeneous objectives despite differences in scale and optimization direction, MORAD maps each measurement to a bounded desirability score and combines them with a weighted geometric mean. title: Framework to identify defect-insensitive electron transport in topological semimetals
authors: Lily Jade Joyce, Michelle M. Kelley et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Topological semimetals are of increasing interest to replace conventional metals for interconnects in future semiconductor chips, due to their potential to exhibit decreasing resistivity with reducing wire dimensions and a lower sensitivity to electron scattering at defects.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: First-principles evaluation of promising topological semimetals for interconnects typically employ non-equilibrium Green's functions (NEGF) techniques to estimate defect scattering, but such calculations for specific defect geometries are difficult to systematize and compare between disparate materials. Here, we develop an NEGF-based approach to systematically and rapidly evaluate the defect sensitivity of electron transport in materials without depending on material-specific defect geometries.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Specifically, we analyze the eigen-spectrum of the transmission matrix for an incoherent ensemble of all-possible single-atom vacancy defects, which clearly reveals eigenvalues close to 1 for defect-insensitive transport modes. Applied to the leading candidates, we show that this robustness to defect scattering is extremely sensitive to surface orientation and Fermi level for each material.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This technique improves the state-of-the-art NEGF method and enables unbiased evaluation of future topological semimetal candidates for nanoscale interconnects.

title: FLaG: Frequency-Domain Latent-attention Gated Pooling for Token Aggregation
authors: Kewei Li, Rongying Zhang et al. (9 researchers)

slides.hook: Token aggregation converts token-level representations into fixed-dimensional sample representations, but most pooling methods operate only in the original token space.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We introduce Frequency-Domain Latent-attention Gated Pooling (FLaG), a plug-in aggregation module that re-expresses encoder outputs in the Fourier domain before final pooling. FLaG represents the nonredundant rFFT spectrum through concatenated real and imaginary components, summarizes spectral tokens with learnable latent queries, derives a sample-conditioned channel gate, and reconstructs modulated token representations for downstream aggregation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We evaluate the same architecture across ESM2-based antimicrobial peptide (AMP) activity prediction, ResNet18 image classification on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and three RoBERTa-based language tasks. FLaG achieves the best macro-averaged Spearman correlation coefficient, RMSE, and Recall@50 across four AMP backbone-species settings and the highest top-1 accuracy on CIFAR 10.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: Supplementary materials, source code, and data are available at https://www.healthinformaticslab.org/supp/ and https://github.com/Kewei2023/AMPCliff/tree/FLaG.

title: Probing quasiperiodic spectral accessibility with a finite-rate quantum Otto cycle
authors: Shujie Cheng, Lucas C. Céleri et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Quasiperiodic systems combine sharply different spectral and localisation regimes with a dense hierarchy of dynamical time scales.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We show that a finite-rate quantum Otto cycle can use this structure as a thermodynamic probe, revealing which parts of the spectrum become dynamically accessible and thermodynamically relevant during a driven transformation. For a generalised Aubry-André-Harper chain, the resulting response is not determined by the static quasiperiodic regime alone: extended, near-critical, and crossing protocols do not exhibit universal ordering of work fluctuations.

title: Multimodal reasoning for broadly neutralizing antibody discovery from label-free human B cell repertoires across virus families
authors: Hantao Lou, Jianqing Zheng et al. (24 researchers)

slides.hook: Discovering broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) from human natural immune repertoires remains a fundamental challenge in immunology, hindered by: the extreme rarity of bnAb, incomplete understanding of their cellular origins across pathogens, and the inability of existing computational tools to generalize across emerging viral threats.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we present ImmuneAgent, a closed-loop AI system that integrates multimodal reasoning with continual meta-learning and wet-lab feedback to overcome these barriers. Applied to screen the natural BCR repertoires from vaccinated or infected cohorts, the system achieves a ~55% neutralization antibody discovery rate (60 of 110 cloned candidates) and a ~11% bnAb yield (12 of 110), substantially outperforming a state-of-the-art sequence-based neutralization predictor or cofolding models evaluated at the same cloning budget.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Five ImmuneAgent-discovered antibodies conferred 100% in vivo protection against lethal influenza challenge, comparable to the clinical-stage therapeutic MEDI8852. The system recovered the cellular and structural determinants of bnAb activity and identified FCRL5+CD27+ atypical memory B cells as a conserved bnAb reservoir and hydrophobic interface enrichment as a cross-viral structural signature, which generalized to unseen antigens, discovering human metapneumovirus (hMPV) cross-neutralizing and human papillomavirus (HPV)-neutralizing antibodies without antigen-specific sorting.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results validate that ImmuneAgent is a generalizable framework for rapid therapeutic antibody discovery against emerging viral threats.

title: Same Luck, Different Choice: Twin-World Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
authors: Zeropy Surio, Tobias Engel et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Agentic reinforcement learning rewards a complete episode, yet the policy needs credit for every decision inside it.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Counterfactual branching estimates this credit by re-running the episode after an alternative decision, but the branch draws its sampling noise independently of the factual episode, so the outcome difference mixes the effect of the decision with the luck of everything that follows. We observe that in agentic search the retriever, the corpus, and the grader are deterministic, so an episode is a deterministic function of the policy's decisions and its sampling noise.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Twin worlds are therefore realizable: the same noise, a different decision. We introduce TWICE (TWIn-world Credit Estimation), which keys the Gumbel noise of every token by turn and line, rolls out counterfactual twins that inherit the factual episode's downstream noise, and turns their paired outcome differences into turn-level advantages for policy-gradient updates on actor-sampled trajectories; only the actor is deployed.

title: Storage-Centric System Designs for Enabling Fast, Efficient, and Low-Cost Genomic and Metagenomic Analyses
authors: Nika Mansouri Ghiasi

slides.hook: Genomic and metagenomic analyses play critical roles in many fields, such as precision medicine, urgent clinical settings, discovering early warnings of communicable diseases, ensuring food safety through pathogen monitoring, agriculture, and scientific discovery.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Due to the challenges of analyzing and storing massive volumes of genomic and metagenomic sequence data, significant efforts have been made to accelerate (meta)genomic analyses and store sequence data compressed. Despite the benefits of these techniques, we identify two major outstanding problems in accessing stored sequence data and supplying it to the analysis units: (i) the data movement bottleneck due to moving large amounts of low-reuse data from storage and the unnecessary burden on the rest of the system, and (ii) the data preparation bottleneck, where compressed sequence data needs to be first decompressed and formatted before analysis.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In this dissertation, we present customized storage-centric systems, which efficiently (i) analyze (meta)genomic data inside the storage system, and (ii) enable highly-compressed storage and high-performance access of large-scale sequence data, thereby alleviating the overheads of data movement, computation, and data preparation. slides.hook: A detection of primordial B modes in the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) polarisation relies on a robust control and removal of contamination from astrophysical polarised foreground emission.

slides.content: For experiments targeting noise levels of order σ_Psimeq 1,μK,{rm arcmin}, we find that masking all ERSs with fluxes above sim0.1 Jy, coupled with a relatively simple model to marginalise over residual point-source contamination, achieves a suitable balance that allows for the robust recovery of unbiased cosmological and foreground parameters at a negligible cost in parameter uncertainties.

slides.hook: Adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration (ADR) based on frustrated rare-earth magnets provides a promising route toward helium-free sub-Kelvin cooling, while balancing magnetic entropy and interaction scales is essential for optimizing the ADR functionalities.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Here we investigate the low-temperature magnetic and ADR properties of the alkali rare-earth double phosphates K_3Ln(PO_4)_2 (Ln = Yb, Gd), which crystallize in a monoclinic P2_1/m structure containing distorted isosceles triangular lattices of rare-earth ions. Crystal-electric-field calculations confirm a J_{mathrm{eff}} = 1/2 ground-state doublet in K_3Yb(PO_4)_2, while thermodynamic analysis based on magnetic entropy and interaction scales accounts for the distinct ADR performance of the two compounds.

slides.hook: Taxonomic classifiers based on exact matches differ in which matches they use and in how each match splits its credit among the taxa containing it: Kraken~2 gives a k-mer's credit to the lowest common ancestor of those taxa, SPUMONI~2 labels each position of the read, Tagger gives each maximal exact match (MEM) one label, and Cliffy splits a match's credit evenly over a roughly logarithmic sample of the taxa.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We compare these schemes on the same long MEMs, mainly on short 16S rRNA reads classified to genera with SILVA, where credit proportional to the number of occurrences of the MEM in each taxon is the most accurate, by 1.0 to 6.8 percentage points. We compute long MEMs with Boyer--Moore--Li on a run-length compressed suffix array, and count their occurrences in each taxon with a complete, run-length compressed tag array, in time proportional to the number of tag runs in the MEM's BWT interval, without locating any occurrence.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We bound the number of tag runs in terms of the BWT runs and of how often suffixes with long common prefixes have different tags, and show that tags constant on d blocks of the text have a macro scheme with at most r + 2d phrases. On SILVA our index takes 1.44,GB and classifies a read in 66,μs with one thread at 93.8% accuracy, about what Cliffy reports for its 9,GB index; over minimizer digests it takes 0.49,GB and reaches 92.5%, against 84.2% for Cliffy's digested index on the same reads.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: On nanopore reads from whole genomes, where almost every long MEM occurs in one species, we instead use each read's longest MEMs, found in one pass of a variant of Boyer--Moore--Li with a k-mer filter, which assigns 99.6% of the reads to their species with no length threshold.

slides.content: We used Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1) images to quantify ICL shapes for 205 clusters at 0.1 leq z leq 0.8 selected from the eROSITA All-Sky Survey and the Dark Energy Survey. title: Evolutionary Architecture Search for Chlorophyll-a Prediction in Lakes using Sentinel-2
authors: Kursat Komurcu & Linas Petkevicius

slides.hook: Small tabular datasets with expert-designed spectral features are the norm in operational Earth observation, and the networks applied to them are typically hand-designed.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We revisit one such published model -- a Sentinel-2 algal bloom classifier -- and ask what architecture search adds, holding the task, the features and the lake-level train/test split of the original study fixed. slides.hook: When insulators are excited by photons with above-gap energies, photo-doped carriers are transiently generated.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Typically, orbital excitations weaken and broaden due to increased screening by these transient carriers, followed by a few-ps recovery via phonon thermalization. Here we report the observation of anomalous dynamics of many-body molecular orbital excitations in the narrow-gap Kondo insulator FeSb_2.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: In the pumped X-ray absorption spectra following excitation with 1~μm photons, we observe a transient transfer of absorption intensity from the delocalized states at the main absorption peak to the localized molecular orbital states at the pre-edge. At the resonance of the low-energy molecular orbital excitations, the pumped resonant inelastic X-ray spectra show an approximately 30% intensity increase at a pump fluence of 11 mJ/cm^2 concomitant with the emergence of an energy gain feature.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These observations require the invocation of a many-body excitation picture beyond single particle population changes.

title: STUART: Sequence Triage and qUAntification of Read Transcripts for Rapid Ionizing Radiation Exposure Assessment
authors: Tomasz Strzoda, Lourdes Cruz-Garcia et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Rapid medical triage following ionizing radiation exposure is critical for emergency management, yet traditional alignment-based bioinformatics are too computationally intensive for mass-casualty scenarios.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: To address this, we developed STUART (Sequence Triage and qUAntification of Read Transcripts), a mapping-free machine learning framework optimized for mobile biological dosimetry. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: While the architecture is universally applicable to any transcriptomic biomarker, this study focused on radiation exposure using the FDXR gene model. title: Confirming candidate self-lensing binary detections with radial velocity measurements
authors: Adam McMaster, Madeline-Mai Ward et al. (9 researchers)

slides.hook: Compact objects in approximately edge-on binary orbits with stars are able to produce a self-lensing effect, amplifying light from their companion once per orbit.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: To date, five white dwarf self-lensing systems are known, while none are known containing black holes or neutron stars. Discovery of such systems is a potential method of finding quiescent black holes and neutron stars, most of which will be pristine and unchanged from their formation.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Photometric detections can suffer from degeneracies in the lens mass and orbital parameters when the amplification and crossing time are not well constrained, while photometric searches produce too many false positives to allow radial velocity investigation of every candidate. Therefore we investigate the minimal radial velocity (RV) observational requirements to characterise such systems by simulating detectable self-lensing light curves, using those light curves to generate targeted RV observations, and fitting RV jointly with photometry.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These results suggest that multi-stage RV follow-up, starting with a small number of observations of many candidates, can efficiently classify self-lensing candidates and identify high-priority systems for further investigation.

title: Delta N-gram: Forward-Only Continual Writing into a Language Model's Native N-gram Memory
authors: Hao Wu

slides.hook: Our previous analysis found that a model's native hashed N-gram table is where continual updates disturb the base least, but its writes needed backpropagation and changed the pretrained table.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We present Delta N-gram, a forward-only write path into that table. The pretrained table T^0 is never modified.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Evidence is written into a sparse patch Δon the rows it addresses: a 4.1M-parameter writer emits a target and a gate per (position, hash head) event, and a block-averaged delta rule keeps each row a convex combination of its old value and the gated targets. The writer is trained offline on raw text with the pretraining objective; at use time writing takes forward passes only, and clearing Δrestores the original model.

title: Constraining Dynamical Dark Energy with Tomographic Galaxy and CMB Weak Lensing Through Higher-Order Statistics

title: How large an effect would we have seen? Positive controls, detection floors and dataset pitfalls in scalp-EEG speech decoding
authors: Blessing Isoyiza Adeika & Onyema Osuagwu

slides.hook: Studies that decode imagined speech from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) commonly validate their pipelines with a positive control, usually overt speech, and report null results without stating what effect size the pipeline could have detected.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Using ds003626 ("Thinking out loud"), KaraOne and Track 3 of the 2020 International Brain-Computer Interface Competition, we audited decoding of overt speech, articulator preparation and imagined speech with artifact-channel subsets, band-limited decoding and trial selection, under a protocol that enforces split integrity by assertion. We injected class-dependent effects of known amplitude into the real recordings to measure the detection floor of five decoder families, and we checked the ds003626 labels against the dataset's acquisition protocol.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: On ds003626, two lip electrodes decoded overt speech at 0.7430 and the eight external channels at 0.7068, against 0.4231 for the 128-channel scalp montage, and no decodable signal survived in the 8-30 Hz band. On the other two corpora, within-subject accuracy rose monotonically with frequency into the range dominated by muscle activity.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Because chunks are embedded independently, a boundary that moves after an edit forces unchanged text to be re-embedded. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: On the 116-article common-success pool, with frozen, length-calibrated parameters, fixed-size chunking recomputes 57-68% of its full new-version embedding-input workload, recursive chunking 38-56%, and content-defined chunking 43-54% (it failed on 4 of 62 Chinese articles), while at these parameters mean evidence recall under a fixed 2048-token retrieval budget differs by less than two percentage points within either language. A cost-only parameter grid shows that the ranking of the two content-aware chunkers changes with chunk-length settings, whereas non-overlapping fixed-size chunking has the highest recomputation cost in every length-matched condition.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints

slides.hook: Trust and reputation mechanisms can reduce the influence of malicious clients in federated learning (FL), but strict update filtering is difficult under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data because honest local updates may temporarily reduce performance on a shared validation proxy.

title: A Catalog of Spectral Properties for DESI DR1 Quasars
authors: Qiaoya Wu & Yue Shen

slides.hook: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) is carrying out a five-year spectroscopic survey designed to map the large-scale structure of the Universe and obtain spectra for millions of galaxies and quasars over a wide redshift range.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We present a value-added catalog of spectral properties for 1,717,774 unique quasars (1,774,723 spectra) in the DESI Data Release 1. slides.hook: We theoretically investigate the interplay of topology and localized non-Hermiticity in a finite Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain characterized by non-Hermitian potentials at its boundaries.

slides.hook: Millimeter-wave and terahertz technologies offer new opportunities for high-capacity communications, sensing, and quantum systems, but electronic signal chains above 100 GHz are limited by weak sources, noisy receivers, and lossy interconnects.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: Photonic approaches mitigate these constraints by enabling chip-scale high-frequency components, yet existing implementations generally retain lossy off-chip electrical or free-space links, hindering dense and compact integration for cryogenic or space-constrained settings. slides.hook: Large-scale models have permeated the molecular sciences, yet what makes a model 'foundational' in this domain remains poorly defined.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: This paper proposes three testable criteria for assessing the foundational nature of molecular models: (i) generality across molecular entities, properties, and tasks; (ii) transferability to new applications with no or minimal task-specific retraining; and (iii) generalization beyond the training distribution. Applying these criteria to the state of the art reveals promising progress, particularly visible in biomolecular structure prediction and machine-learned interatomic potentials, although none of the approaches examined fully satisfies all three.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Success is concentrated in domains where target properties are consistently defined and training data are abundant, with low label noise relative to physically meaningful variation. More broadly, progress in the molecular sciences appears to depend less on model scale alone than on the quality and structure of available data, as well as the incorporation of prior knowledge into models, prediction tasks, or downstream applications.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: This work shifts the notion of a molecular foundation model from a descriptive label to a testable hypothesis, offering a framework for assessing current models and guiding future developments.

title: MerKurio: sequence extraction and annotation based on matching k-mers
authors: Lukas Schönmann, Heinz Himmelbauer et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: K-mers, short subsequences of length k, play an important role in computational analyses using biological sequence data.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: A critical downstream processing step involves getting back to the source sequences of selected k-mers for further analysis or validation. Here, we present MerKurio, a high-performance command line tool written in Rust with two main functionalities: 1) extracting sequence records from FASTA/FASTQ files using k-mers and 2) annotating or filtering aligned sequences in SAM/BAM files with k-mer tags.

title: CancerZigZag: Iterative Seed-Anchored Diffusion for Generative Modeling of Single-Cell State Transitions

slides.hook: Single-cell cancer datasets are predominantly cross-sectional and rarely provide paired or longitudinal observations linking individual healthy-like cells to tumor-associated states.

title: Superconducting weak links at substrate steps in bilayer nickelate films

slides.content: We show that these features arise from superconducting weak links at substrate step-terrace structures. slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence

authors: Sachin Gupta

title: Zero-Shot Forecasting of In-Situ Soil Moisture and Temperature with a Time-Series Foundation Model
authors: Mohammad Talaei, Mohammad Goudarzi et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Soil moisture and temperature govern plant-water availability and microbial activity, making them key indicators for evaluating land-restoration efforts on degraded landscapes.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, the physical and data-driven models normally used to forecast them both need information that a newly instrumented restoration site does not yet have: hydraulic parameters for the former and months of per-site training data for the latter. We evaluate TimesFM 1, a 500M-parameter time-series foundation model, zero-shot on 15-minute telemetry from 27 sensor stations across three land-management regimes (Control, Treatment, Scald) at a semi-arid restoration site, forecasting 5 cm and 30 cm soil moisture and enclosure temperature at seven lead times from 1 h to 168 h.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Using gap-aware rolling-origin evaluation across sensors, we find that TimesFM beats the best rule-based statistical forecasting baselines (persistence, seasonal-naive, or 7-day climatology) by 21-76% at sub-daily lead times but loses by 6-79% beyond a day, a pattern explained by a diurnal-alignment mechanism that holds for both soil-moisture depths and temperature. title: Benchmarking Recent Single-Cell Synthetic Data Generation Methods on the OneK1K Dataset
authors: Buse Giledereli, Basar Temiz et al. (3 researchers)

slides.hook: Synthetic single-cell RNA-seq data generation offers a promising route for privacy-aware biomedical data sharing, but donor-linked datasets require careful balancing of biological utility and privacy risk.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: In this work, we benchmark synthetic generation methods for the CAMDA 2026 ELSA Health Privacy Challenge using the donor-split OneK1K dataset, comparing scGFT, scLDM, and Cell2Sentence across statistical fidelity, downstream biological preservation, and membership inference vulnerability. Because full-transcriptome generation is computationally demanding, we focus generative modeling on highly variable genes and evaluate alternative strategies for reconstructing non-HVG expression.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: Our results show that non-HVG handling is a central determinant of privacy: directly copying non-HVG values leads to severe leakage, whereas Poisson-based reconstruction substantially reduces membership inference risk. We further find that scGFT and scLDM better preserve biological structure than an independent Poisson baseline, while maintaining near-random privacy profiles under appropriate configurations.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: These findings highlight the importance of evaluating synthetic single-cell data beyond marginal similarity alone, emphasizing robustness, interpretability, and privacy-conscious design choices throughout preprocessing, generation, and post-processing.

title: Microscopically informed self-consistent multi-resolvent closure for dense many-body spectra
authors: Zhiqiang Huang

slides.hook: The exact multi-resolvent hierarchy of dense many-body spectra encodes higher-order spectral-weight correlations, but closing it predictively for interacting Hamiltonians remains a challenge.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We introduce the multi-resolvent self-consistency (MRSC) equations, which separate an exact algebraic hierarchy from an approximate finite-parameter closure. title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues
authors: Yancheng Zhu & Yifan Yuan

slides.hook: Large language models can repeat an instruction while failing to keep obeying it.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: We study this recall-compliance dissociation in long-horizon dialogue and define State Integrity Collapse: a model preserves a stated constraint in memory but stops applying it to later turns. title: Dealing with low-weight errors that lead BP OSD to fail
authors: Giacomo Fregona, Matthias C. Löbl et al. (5 researchers)

slides.hook: Belief Propagation combined with Ordered Statistics Decoding (BP OSD) is an open-source decoding tool used widely within the community due to its versatility and ease of application to Quantum Low Density Parity Check (QLDPC) codes.

slides.title: Methodological Architecture & Specifications
slides.content: However, the degeneracy of quantum codes has been observed to degrade the performance of BP OSD, particularly leading to error floors for low physical error rates. Here, we investigate the low-weight error configurations responsible for such failures in Bivariate Bicycle codes.

slides.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Evidence
slides.content: We show that, at code capacity, BP OSD fails on errors whose weight is significantly smaller than d/2, arising from global symmetries of the decoding graph that prevent the convergence of parallel BP. Furthermore, our analysis reveals new pitfalls that can arise when analysing the performance of BP OSD in the rare events regime, such as loss of ergodicity in splitting methods and numerical instabilities in the decoder.

slides.title: Critical Frontier & Open Constraints
slides.content: We show how to mitigate these failure mechanisms by modifying the BP update rules and the decoder implementation, leading to substantial improvement in logical error rate.
